rules.message: Because your ALT was {v} U/L on {date}, above the healthy limit of {uln}, the plan favours steady fat loss and less sugar.
Because your ALT was {v} U/L on {date}, the plan keeps alcohol to {cap} g a day or less. Less is better for the liver.
Heavy or new lifting can raise ALT and AST for a week. Did you train hard in the 7 days before {date}?
Because your ALT was {v} U/L on {date}, the plan keeps the surplus small. Big surpluses raise ALT within weeks.
Because your ALT was {v} U/L on {date}: green tea extract and ashwagandha can rarely injure the liver. Consider pausing it and retesting.
Because your ALT was {v} U/L on {date}, more than 3 times your lab's limit, please see a clinician. The plan stays gentle until then.
Retest ALT around {date+12w} to see whether the plan is helping. Avoid hard lifting for 7 days before.
Because your AST was {v} U/L on {date}: did you lift hard or start new training in the 7 days before? Muscle can raise AST for a week.
Retest AST and ALT around {date+12w}, with no hard lifting in the 7 days before.
Because your AST was {v} U/L on {date}, more than 3 times your lab's limit, please see a clinician.
Because your GGT was {v} U/L on {date}, which often rises with alcohol, how much do you usually drink in a week?
Because your GGT was {v} U/L on {date}, the plan cuts alcohol. GGT usually falls within 2–3 weeks of drinking less.
Retest GGT around {date+6w}. If it is still high after weeks of little or no alcohol, see a clinician.
Your GGT stayed high on {date} after weeks of little alcohol. Please see a clinician to check your liver.
Because your eGFR was {v} on {date}, the plan keeps protein at or below 1.3 g per kg a day, as kidney guidelines advise.
Because your eGFR was {v} on {date}, we don't suggest creatine or potassium salt. Ask your doctor before using them.
A single low eGFR is not a diagnosis. Retest around {date+3m}, without cooked meat that morning and off creatine for 2 weeks.
Because your eGFR was {v} on {date}, check with your doctor before keto or fasts over 24 h (kidney stones, fluid and salt shifts).

Because your urine ACR was {v} mg/g on {date}, the plan favours less salt and steady weight loss, which lower it.
Because your ACR was {v} mg/g on {date}: keto raises kidney-stone risk (about 8 in 100 adults). Drink well and check with your doctor.
Because your urine ACR was {v} mg/g on {date}, severely increased, please see a clinician soon.
